intendedFunction: A broad two-adult oak settle beside the main hall hearth, with a stable vertical rear frame, correctly proportioned seat, and draught-screening paneled back.
prompt: Author a cohesive late-medieval two-seat oak hearth settle from a dimensioned human seating section. Use plumb lower rear legs, a separate upper back frame raked four degrees away from the occupant on one common construction plane, a 460 mm seat height, 500 mm physical seat depth, 700 mm arm height, one continuous 1820 mm seat plank, continuous framed fielded-panel back, visible mortise-and-tenon shoulders, and drawbore pegs. Do not rake the lower legs and do not segment the seat into occupant-width slabs.

cues.statement: Scale the documented 70 by 41.5 by 23 inch reference envelope without changing its low broad ratios.
The usable seat is dimensioned before the back and ornament, supporting two adults without reading as a shelf or three cushions.
Plumb lower rear legs support a distinct upper frame raked four degrees away from the occupant; every upper back member derives from the same section line.
Four fields sit within a continuous rail-and-stile frame and cannot read as loose boards.
Rails enter the correct front or rear posts with visible shoulders and drawbore pegs.
The settle must remain visibly shared seating from front and three-quarter views.
